For a postcard like this, here are the standard technical specs used in the print and design industry:

**Standard sizes** (most common for direct mail/wedding stationery)
- 4" × 6" — most common, cheapest to print, fits standard postcard postage
- 5" × 7" — popular for wedding save-the-dates specifically, feels more substantial
- 6" × 9" or 6" × 11" — jumbo, used for real estate/marketing where standout matters

Your design's 3:2 aspect ratio matches the classic 4"×6" or 6"×9" format well.

**Resolution & color**
- **300 DPI** at final print size (industry standard for sharp print — 72–150 DPI will look soft/pixelated in print, even if it looks fine on screen)
- **CMYK color mode**, not RGB — printers use CMYK, and colors (especially your sage greens and dusty pinks) can shift noticeably if left in RGB. Convert before sending to print.
- So at 4"×6" and 300 DPI, your working file should be **1200×1800px** minimum; at 5"×7" it's **1500×2100px**.

**Bleed & safe margin**
- **0.125" (1/8") bleed** on all sides — extend your background/botanical elements past the trim line so no white edge shows if trimming is slightly off.
- **0.125"–0.25" safe margin** inside the trim line — keep text and important elements (like "[name 1] & [name 2]") inboard of this so nothing gets clipped.

**File format for print**
- Deliver as **PDF (print-ready, with bleed marks)** or a flattened **high-res TIFF/PSD** — not PNG/JPG for final print handoff, since those often get compressed and lose CMYK accuracy.

**If this will actually be mailed (USPS postcard rules)**
- Min: 3.5" × 5", Max: 4.25" × 6" for postcard-rate postage; anything larger gets charged as a letter or large envelope rate. Also needs to be rectangular and between 0.007"–0.016" thick.

**For your Upwork thumbnail specifically**
- None of the print specs above matter for the thumbnail itself — Upwork will just display whatever image you upload, so a clean 1600×1200px (or similar) PNG/JPG at screen resolution (72–150 DPI) is completely fine. The print specs above only matter if a client will actually take this to a printer.
